The hypothesis names a specific, controllable mechanism rather than restating the symptom: 'The corrective guidance and the allowlist that governs what a reviewer may read are two different surfaces, and only one of them was updated ... path_is_authorized was never extended to admit the artifact that document tells reviewers to inspect, and no test compares the two.' That is a process mechanism (divergent surfaces with no parity check), not a restatement of 'the check cannot be performed'. Caveat recorded, not charged here: the sub-condition that the hypothesis be the terminal cause of the '## Why-Why Analysis' chain could not be evaluated because that section is absent entirely; the absence is charged once, under WHY-CHAIN-VALID, and the chain proposed in this audit's revisions terminates at exactly this mechanism.

The WFI contains no '## Why-Why Analysis' section at all: the document proceeds directly from '## Root Cause Hypothesis' to '## Proposed Change' (verified by header scan; the only 'Why' in the file is a column header inside the Problem Evidence step table). A missing section is a Major finding by rule 1 of this check; a why-why chain of at least 3 evidence-cited levels, anchored on the T-004 cycle-3 identity block and terminating at the stated two-surfaces mechanism, must be added on revision. The raw material for every level already exists in the WFI's own Problem Evidence and Root Cause Hypothesis, so this is an omission of form, not of substance — see proposed revision 1.

Shared plugins/-path rule, applied on identical conditions as NO-PLUGIN-SCOPE-CREEP: the described targets resolve to plugins/ files, and the carve-out is NOT applied because its condition 2 is unmet (see that check); naming the literal paths is nevertheless the correct revision, paired with the '## Category' statement that activates the carve-out.

The '## Expected Effect' section reads: 'A reviewer can verify its own launch identity to the strength the boundary reference claims, using evidence it is actually given. Today it can verify one of four properties and must take the other three on the launching agent's word...' This names no metric and states no quantitative target within the section. The 'one of four properties' phrasing gestures at a number but never states the target state or the metric that will register it; both requirements of this check are unmet inside this section. The needed content already exists one section down ('metrics.reviewer_identity_boundary_blocks', baseline 2, target 0 of 10), so this is a wording defect: restate the metric name and the numeric targets (2 -> 0 of the next 10 launches; 1-of-4 -> 4-of-4 verifiable properties) inside '## Expected Effect' itself — see proposed revision 4.
